rationale: All seven of my round-1 concrete asks are ADDRESSED at 8a13b898, each re-derived against the tree rather than taken from the fix report. (1) R1.3 now names the three surfaces per row and carries an explicit plan-approve carve-out for OQ-3 option 2 (annotated stored/derived pair instead of a false three-way agreement), and AC-2 asserts those surfaces — the round-1 masking (testing only the derivation, the one surface that agreed with the row) is gone. (2) The main-checkout shape got a full disposition and more: settled fact 6 now reproduces BOTH prior observations with the bd-availability discriminator (I checked derive.go:588-597's err==nil-guarded arms match the claimed mechanism), and R1.4 + three-leg AC-1 pin both main-checkout legs with captured red-on-revert counterexamples. (3) R6.3(a-c) makes every filter drop loud on every path, AC-10 gains the partial-exclusion assertion, AC-10b pins the empty-after-filter case red-on-revert, and the Non-Goals #255 entry now names exactly which face moved in and which stays deferred — the boundary is precise. (4) AC-14 covers all nine R2.1 verbs table-driven. (5) AC-7 has the mixed-commit leg and the paths-only pin with 'tool-authored' deliberately dropped and the any-actor residual asserted (leg iii) plus the non-listed-.beads-path leg (iv); I verified artifactPaths is exactly ['.beads/issues.jsonl'] at guard.go:24-26. (6) The G8 resolution is the strong form of my ask: the claim-written enumeration was DERIVED empty (I verified .mindspec/session.json at .gitignore:3) and the block removal is said out loud, with AC-8(ii)'s enumeration-pinning re-arm test and AC-8(iii)'s seam leg keeping the refusal machinery falsifiable. (7) OQ-5 is narrowed to the default-pick rule, its mischaracterization of AC-9 is corrected, and AC-9 now asserts the default-line. New material also survives scrutiny: AC-9's single-item red-on-revert claim is grounded (select.go:20-22 early return verified), and AC-5(v)'s 'existing' derivation seam is real (derive.go:46-64 runBDFn/listJSONFn). Four MINOR wording-precision residuals remain (below), none a hidden design foreclosure and each a one-to-two-line fix; the requirement text, Impacted Domains, and Scope already carry the correct conditionals in every case, so these do not warrant another blocked round.
concrete_changes_required: AC-7(iii): scope it explicitly to OQ-1(c) (e.g. 'under OQ-1(c) only: a delta confined to ...'), and add the same tag to AC-6's diff-pathspec sentence. As written, leg (iii) asserts exemption behavior that exists only if the plan chooses (c), while OQ-1 still claims 'R4's ACs are written to hold under any of (a)/(b)/(c)' — under (a)/(b) there is no exemption and leg (iii) is unsatisfiable. R4.2, Impacted Domains, and Scope all conditionalize on (c) correctly; only the AC text lags. Legs (i)/(ii)/(iv) are genuinely arm-independent and need no change.

R1.3 / AC-2: state the tail-less carve-out for the `release` row the way the plan-approve carve-out is stated. R2.1 records that `release` emits no instruct tail (its result line satisfies the ordering requirement), but R1.3's agreement-table contract has each row's fixture assert three surfaces including 'the emitted instruct tail's selected template' — unrunnable for a verb with no tail. The generic 'per-row carve-outs stated in the table itself' clause covers it in spirit; name it so AC-2's fixture obligation for that row is well-defined.

AC-14: drop or mechanize the second permitted anti-drift arm. 'A count sentinel plus an in-diff extension obligation' does not make 'adding a durable-state-mutating verb without a row' red — a new verb added elsewhere leaves a hardcoded list and its count untouched, and the extension obligation is a process hope, not a failing test. Only the first arm (enumerate the cobra commands that reach a mutation seam) delivers the AC's own red-on-add claim; require that arm.

AC-4: one clause scoping sentence — the agreement-with-Result.NextMode assertion applies exactly when context resolution succeeds; the indeterminate-marker branch applies exactly when it does not. As written, a tail that always renders the indeterminate marker arguably satisfies both clauses (round-1 MINOR, unconsolidated, unchanged at this commit).

findings.title: AC-7(iii) and AC-6's pathspec assertion are OQ-1(c)-conditional but not marked so, contradicting OQ-1's arm-independence claim
findings.detail: OQ-1 retains 'R4's ACs are written to hold under any of (a)/(b)/(c)', but AC-7(iii) positively asserts a staleness exemption ('a delta confined to the named artifact file is exempt regardless of who authored it') that exists only under arm (c) — under (a) the tool never creates the post-review delta and under (b) it removes it, so any post-review tracker-only commit (e.g. an external one) still trips the unchanged stale-SHA gate and leg (iii)'s test is unwritable. AC-6's 'delta the gate ignored was confined to the named artifact set' is the same defect in vacuous form (empty diff under (a)/(b)). Everything around the ACs is conditionalized correctly (R4.2's 'if the chosen mechanism involves a staleness-exemption fact — and only then', internal/panel marked CONDITIONAL in Impacted Domains and Scope), and AC-7's preamble 'matching the paths-only pin' — a pin R4.2 defines as 'if taken' — offers a defensible conditional reading, which is why this is MINOR rather than a hidden foreclosure. One scoping tag per AC closes it.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE from fix: R1.3's new release row conflicts with R2.1's release-emits-no-tail fact
findings.detail: The fix added 'release → implement / plan' rows to the agreement table (correctly matched to ADR-0023's amended :140 row and all-open :142 row against derive.go's lifecycleClosed>0/all-open branches), but R1.3's row contract makes each fixture assert three surfaces including 'the emitted instruct tail's selected template', while R2.1 (also new this round) records that release emits no tail today. AC-2's obligation for the release row is therefore unrunnable as written. The generic per-row carve-out clause exists; state the tail-less carve-out for release explicitly, as was done for plan-approve.

findings.title: AC-14's count-sentinel arm does not deliver its own red-on-add claim
findings.detail: AC-14 claims 'Adding a durable-state-mutating verb without a row is red' but permits two mechanisms, and the second — 'pins the list with a count sentinel plus an in-diff extension obligation' — is not red when a new mutating verb is added elsewhere: a hardcoded list and its count are untouched, and the extension obligation is unmechanized process text. Only the first arm (enumerate cobra commands reaching a mutation seam) is falsifiable in the promised direction. Since the AC lets the implementation choose the weaker arm, the promise can be satisfied vacuously; require the enumeration arm.

findings.title: AC-4 clause scoping still open (round-1 residual, not in the consolidated asks)
findings.detail: AC-4 gained the ADR-0035 recovery-line leg (G6.3) but the round-1 MINOR about clause scoping is unchanged: nothing states that the agrees-with-Result.NextMode assertion applies exactly when context resolution succeeds and the indeterminate branch exactly when it fails, so an always-indeterminate tail arguably satisfies both. One sentence making the two conditions disjoint closes it. Classification: this was a round-1 finding of mine but not one of my seven concrete asks, and the consolidation evidently did not carry it — recorded here so it is fixed or refuted rather than dropped.
